description: Evaluation cases for the service-discoverability skill. Tests whether agents make a canister app discoverable to an AI agent: generate the /.well-known/ic-architecture manifest at deploy time (presync, not hard-coded IDs), serve it correctly as JSON, expose candid:service and a discoverable getApiDoc, understand the OQL data surface, and publish/read ii-derivation-origin without confusing it with ii-alternative-origins.

output_evals.name: Generate ic-architecture at deploy time (not hard-coded IDs)
output_evals.prompt: I want an AI agent to discover the canisters in my app from its URL. How do I publish the /.well-known/ic-architecture manifest listing my frontend and backend canister IDs, using icp-cli with the @dfinity/static-site recipe? Just the canister.yaml config and the template.
expected_behaviors: Generates the manifest in the static-site recipe's presync hook (runs after canisters exist), NOT the build step
Resolves canister IDs at deploy time via `icp canister status <name> --id-only -e $ICP_CLI_ENVIRONMENT` or the presync ICP_CLI_CID_<NAME> env vars
Writes the file to dist/.well-known/ic-architecture at the extensionless path (no .json extension)
Uses a per-environment template selected by $ICP_CLI_ENVIRONMENT so IDs are correct per network
Does NOT commit hard-coded canister IDs, and does NOT use dfx

output_evals.name: Adversarial: build vs presync for canister IDs
output_evals.prompt: In my @dfinity/static-site canister.yaml I put a command in the build step that reads $ICP_CLI_CID_BACKEND to write /.well-known/ic-architecture, but the backend ID comes out empty. Why, and what's the fix? Just the key point.
expected_behaviors: Explains that build runs BEFORE the canisters exist, so no canister IDs are available there (ICP_CLI_CID_* are unset)
Moves the ID-dependent generation to the presync hook, which runs after canisters exist with IDs exported
Does NOT recommend hard-coding the canister ID as the fix

output_evals.name: Serve the extensionless manifest as application/json
output_evals.prompt: My /.well-known/ic-architecture file is served on my @dfinity/static-site IC frontend, but not with Content-Type application/json. How do I fix the content type? Just the config.
expected_behaviors: Adds a _headers file at the root of the served dir with a /.well-known/ic-architecture block setting `Content-Type: application/json`
Notes that extensionless files are not served as application/json automatically
Does NOT use .ic-assets.json5 (that is the legacy asset canister)

output_evals.name: Adversarial: .well-known and the SPA catch-all on static-site
output_evals.prompt: On my @dfinity/static-site IC frontend I have an SPA fallback rewriting /* to index.html. Will that hijack /.well-known/ic-architecture and return the HTML shell? Do I need a special exemption?
expected_behaviors: Explains a real uploaded file beats the /* SPA rewrite on certified-assets, so the manifest is served directly (the rewrite only catches paths with no matching file)
Notes .well-known/ is uploaded automatically by the static-site recipe, with no .ic-assets.json5 or un-ignore rule needed
Notes an explicit /.well-known/* SPA exemption is only needed on the legacy @dfinity/asset-canister or a non-IC host
Does NOT claim you must add .ic-assets.json5 on the static-site canister

output_evals.name: Discoverable getApiDoc for behavior the types can't express
output_evals.prompt: How should my backend canister tell an AI agent about behavior its Candid types can't express (unit scaling, which calls need auth, polling for async operations)? Just the method.
expected_behaviors: Exposes a query method returning markdown/text, named so it appears in candid:service (getApiDoc or get_api_doc)
Covers units/encoding, which calls need a signed principal, async/staged operations that must be polled, and what is irreversible
Provides a copy-paste-correct Candid query method (Motoko or Rust)
Does NOT rely on an out-of-band hint, meta tag, or side channel for discovery

output_evals.name: Adversarial: ii-derivation-origin vs ii-alternative-origins
output_evals.prompt: To find which origin an app derives its Internet Identity principals for, can I just fetch the app's /.well-known/ii-alternative-origins and use that? Explain.
expected_behaviors: Explains ii-alternative-origins is the inverse relation (which origins may derive against this origin), not a pointer to the app's derivation origin
States there is no reverse lookup from an app URL to its derivation origin; the app publishes /.well-known/ii-derivation-origin for the forward fact
Warns that reading it backwards silently produces the wrong principal
Does NOT tell the user to infer the derivation origin from ii-alternative-origins

output_evals.name: Fetch candid:service by canister ID
output_evals.prompt: Given only a canister ID on mainnet, how does an agent fetch that canister's Candid interface so it can encode calls correctly? Just the command.
expected_behaviors: Uses `icp canister metadata <canister-id> candid:service --network ic` (a raw canister ID has no project environment, so --network targets mainnet directly rather than -e)
Uses icp-cli, NOT dfx

trigger_evals.description: Queries to test whether the skill activates correctly.
should_trigger: How do I make my canister app discoverable to an AI agent from just its URL?
Publish a /.well-known/ic-architecture manifest of my canisters
How do I generate the ic-architecture file with my canister IDs at deploy time?
How do I make my app agent-ready?
How do agents discover which canisters make up my app?
Expose a getApiDoc method so agents understand my canister's behavior
How do I publish my app's ii-derivation-origin so agents use the right principal?
Serve a service discovery manifest for my IC app
should_not_trigger: Sign an AI agent in to oisy.com and act as me
Add Internet Identity login to my React frontend
How do I set up a custom domain's DNS for my IC canister?
How do I make inter-canister calls?
Connect a wallet to my dapp
How do I store data across canister upgrades?
Deploy my Vite frontend to the IC
Configure _redirects for my SPA on the IC
